extracted.intended_audience: readers and scholars of early modern English biography, colonial American history, and bibliographical studies
extracted.subtask_description: A biographical and bibliographical account of Thomas Hariot, his role in Raleigh's Virginia enterprise, and the provenance/authenticity of associated voyage illustrations and reports. Emphasizes primary sources, drawings, maps, and the bibliographical history behind published collections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complementarity of text and illustrations
rubrics_metrics.description: “Hariot’s text and map with White’s drawings are necessary complements to each other and should be mentioned together.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating or republishing voyage reports, include both the textual survey/map and the original drawings (maps/paintings) as they jointly convey the complete information; omission of one diminishes the work’s completeness and authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authenticity and trustworthiness of De Bry’s collections
rubrics_metrics.description: “Both parts are therefore perfectly authentic and trustworthy.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess the authenticity of multi-author collections (e.g., De Bry’s Peregrinations) by tracing their sources, dedications, and the provenance of the contributing materials; explicit linkage to original materials (Raleigh, Hakluyt, White, Le Moyne, Hariot) supports claims of authenticity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compare engravings to original drawings to judge fidelity
rubrics_metrics.description: “Whoever compares the original drawings of Le Moyne and White with the engravings of De Bry ... must be convinced that, beautiful as De Bry’s work is, it seems tame in the presence of the original water-colour drawings. There is no exaggeration in the engravings.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Direct comparison of originals (e.g., water-colour drawings) with published engravings is necessary to judge whether engravings exaggerate, distort, or faithfully reproduce originals; such comparisons are an evidentiary basis for asserting accuracy or otherwise of published plates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of new contemporary evidence to revise historical estimates
rubrics_metrics.description: The text advocates bringing “new and important contemporary evidence” to light that is “sufficient ... to considerably modify our general estimate of Hariot’s life and character.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Historiographical evaluation should prioritize recovery and publication of contemporary primary evidence (letters, manuscripts, drawings) which may require reopening scholarly debate and revising prior assessments based on earlier secondary accounts (e.g., Anthony a Wood).

rubrics_metrics.name: Bibliographical/provenance inquiry as part of historical evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: The narrative emphasizes the bibliographical history and the intimacy and dependence of persons engaged (Hakluyt, De Bry, Le Moyne, White, Hariot) as intertwined elements leading to Hariot’s biography.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Careful bibliographical and provenance study — tracking publication history, stationers' entries, dedications, ownership (e.g., Sloane collection, British Museum acquisitions) — is essential to establish origin, authority, and context for historical materials and their interpretations.
